# Synthetic comparison contract

## Question

Does the supplied candidate meet the fixed improvement rule against the supplied baseline?

## Question alignment

- Governing question source: research/questions/Q.md#mechanism
- Governing mechanism: Combining complementary logical components may improve generated programs.
- This task tests: The organization increment after both arms receive the same records.
- This task does not decide: Whether complementary components improve generated programs.

## Scope

Inspect only the synthetic aggregate observations. Baseline B0 and candidate C1 use the same fictional evaluation set. This task recomputes one error difference; it does not reproduce predictions, training, or uncertainty estimates.

## Constraints

Error is lower-is-better. Gain is B0 error minus C1 error. Promotion requires gain at least 0.01 absolute error units. Use the supplied aggregate directly, with no seed selection or alternative aggregation. Budget: local standard-library arithmetic only; no network, dependency download, or new experiment.

## Stop conditions

Stop with a bounded answer when arithmetic and interpretation are checked. A negative result is a valid completion. Changing the threshold or collecting new observations requires a separate task. Inconsistent input prevents closure until corrected.

# Synthetic comparison result

## Outcome

C1 does not meet the promotion rule. Its error is higher than B0, and the gain is −0.03 absolute error units, below the required +0.01.

This finding assesses the organization increment after both arms receive the same records. Retain B0 within this fictional comparison.

## Evidence

The supplied [metrics](evidence/metrics.json) mark the observations as synthetic and error as lower-is-better: B0 = 0.20, C1 = 0.23, minimum gain = 0.01. [Derived evidence](evidence/derived.json) correctly records 0.20 − 0.23 = −0.03 and promote = false. The accepted [arithmetic check](check_arithmetic.py) checks the gain and promotion label during managed verification.

The [governing question](../../research/questions/Q.md#mechanism) and related [organization-only route](../../research/ROUTES.md#organization-only-comparison) identify the same-records boundary. The evidence supports the decision to decline C1 promotion under the fixed rule; the broader component-complementarity question remains unanswered.

## Deviations

None in the specified synthetic assessment; the threshold and inputs are unchanged.

## Next action

Retain B0 within this fictional comparison and close the assessment after both required checks pass. There is no authorized extra experiment.

## Limitations

All observations are synthetic aggregates. They establish no real model performance, prediction quality, uncertainty, or general scientific conclusion. This organization-only comparison does not isolate complementary components and neither supports nor refutes whether combining complementary logical components improves generated programs.

checks.rationale: Inspected all four required references against accepted contract revision 1. evidence/metrics.json supplies synthetic lower-is-better errors B0=0.20 and C1=0.23 and minimum_gain=0.01. evidence/derived.json correctly records gain=-0.03 and promote=false. result.md applies baseline minus candidate and the unchanged threshold, declines C1 promotion, and confines the finding to supplied synthetic aggregates and the organization increment with identical records. ../../research/questions/Q.md explains that this comparison does not isolate component complementarity; the result explicitly leaves that mechanism unanswered and neither supports nor refutes it. AC-02 passes on this inspected content; this is an agent judgment.
